## The problem

RM pro has a firmware issue that causes it to return -7 ºC when we call check_sensors() around 22.9 and 23 ºC.

If we ignore the issue, we return unreliable data. If we add a conditional and raise an exception, we raise false positives (-7 ºC may be a valid temperature), and it would also flood the logs, this behavior is consistent.

The right place to fix this is the firmware, but we don't have access to it.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Add a conditional to the update manager and replace -7 with the previous temperature when the variation is bigger than 3 °C.

If we get -7 °C at startup, we return None, so the temperature will be unknown until we get a different value, from which it will be possible to determine whether the next -7 is valid or not.

<!--

- Integration causing this issue: Broadlink
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/broadlink

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Hi. Thanks for reporting this.

A little bit of history. This is an [old issue](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/5439) that Daniel fixed [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/6051) with a validation schema. I recently removed the schema and implemented a [checksum](https://github.com/mjg59/python-broadlink/pull/410) in the library in hopes of fixing it at the protocol level, but now we know it didn't work. The device is indeed sending the wrong information, it is not a problem of corrupted data.

The question is why always 249 degrees? I will investigate this when I find some time. If we don't find a better way, we can bring the validation schema back.
I had the very same issue with my rm3 and it is always the same value (249). Some days it occurs 3 or 4 times a day.
Hello, same issure here RM Pro
Hello, I have the same problem too. I published it in the community but no one has assisted me with the problem

Looks like a firmware issue. It always occurs around 22.9 ºC. The temperature should be:

```python3
b'\x14\x1d'  # 22.9
```
or
```python3
b'\x14\x1e'  # 23.0
```
But we get:
```python3
b'\xf9\x00'  # 249.0 (or -7.0)
```

For Broadlink A1 the temperature is 242.1 (or -13.9).

I will bring the validation back.

Related issues:
https://github.com/frankjoke/ioBroker.broadlink2/issues/32
https://github.com/lprhodes/homebridge-broadlink-rm/issues/319
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/5439

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
This is still an open issue that hasn't been resolved yet.  It still is currently occurring on version 2021.2.3.

Hi @VinnieNZ. Sorry for making you wait so long. We were in the middle of a huge update so I had to focus.

I added another checksum to the library, now we are checking the encrypted data packet. It's not released yet, I hope it will fix. This is my last try before implementing a dirty solution. I don't like the validation schema because it discards negative temperatures. If the new checksum doesn't fix, I will catch the temperature -7 and send a retry when it happens.

I don't know what is the state of this bug, but on 2021.4.3 (and 2021.4.1) it stopped the 249 reports, but started to report -7 instead. 

Any update what's the plan with this issue?

Hi. It's not fixed yet. The -7 is because now we can read negative temperatures (249 is actually -7).

I have a new version of the broadlink module for testing. I added a checksum to the encrypted data packet. Hopefully it will fix this issue. If not, I will fix it another way. If anyone wants to help with the tests:

1. Open Home Assistant and install "SSH & Web Terminal" add-on
2. Disable Protection mode
3. Click "Terminal" on the sidebar and install the patch:
```
docker exec -it homeassistant /bin/bash
pip3 install git+https://github.com/felipediel/python-broadlink.git@test-proto --force-reinstall --no-deps
```
4. Restart the server.

> @felipediel, I was running your fix since the morning and just had a look, and it is still producing -7.
> 

Damn, I just wanted to suggest why not just drop the -7 values, but this device is more tough than I thought.

Specs:


Features | IR frequency: 38K; RF frequency: 433 / 315MHz; **Working temperature: -20'C~60'C;** Working humidity: <=80%; Wireless power consumption: <=0.5W; Wireless type: Wi-Fi 2.4GHz IEEE 802.11b/g/n;
-- | --

Yes, solving this without causing other problems is harder than it seems because we are doing it in the wrong place (this is a firmware issue). I was thinking of adding a function to discard ridiculous variations, but what if we get -7 at startup?

I will update the test to log the problematic packets, maybe we can find a way to filter them.

> I was thinking of adding a function to discard ridiculous variations, but what if we get -7 at startup?

I have thought about that as well, and ended up with the same issue as you mention, what if startup.
Ok, I changed that PR to log malformed packets. Let's see if we can find something different. Please update and send me the log message when you see it.

I've seen several instances of the -7 result, thought I had malformed data logs to send, but it appears they were IR remote commands.

Where is the log hiding?  I can't find anything logged in the output of "docker-compose logs".
Thank you! Apart from -7, the packets are perfect. There is no way to differentiate them :(

If I re-run the below, will I get the fixed version to test?

```
docker exec -it homeassistant /bin/bash
pip3 install git+https://github.com/felipediel/python-broadlink.git@fix-rmpro-sensor --force-reinstall --no-deps
```

No, you need this:
